issue.title: sase publication-outcome test fails in long checkout paths because Rich wraps the repository path
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-jf.1.2 (note #4) while verifying the SASE checkout-identity guard; triaged by the bob-cli-jf.1 lander. This is in the sase repository (`sase repo open sase`).

## What is wrong

`tests/test_commit_workflow_publication_outcomes.py::test_publication_without_target_warns_but_keeps_primary_successful` fails at its output assertion (~line 308 on sase origin/master a14bffcdbf) whenever the checkout path is long, such as SASE workspace paths like `~/.local/state/sase/workspaces/<org>/<project>/<project>_<N>/sase/repos/external/projects/sase`:

```python
output = " ".join(capsys.readouterr().out.split())
assert f"skipped for repository {os.getcwd()!r}" in output
```

Rich wraps the warning at the console width, and the wrap can fall inside the repository path. Whitespace normalization then turns that line break into a space inside the path, so the contiguous `repr(os.getcwd())` is never found. With short checkout paths the test passes, which is why it looks fine elsewhere.

## Fix

Make the assertion independent of wrapping. For example, patch the console width wide or render without wrapping in the test, or compare against the output with all whitespace removed on both sides. Alternatively, make the warning itself print the path with `soft_wrap`/`no_wrap` if unwrapped paths are wanted in real output too. Confirm the fix with a long `tmp_path`-based cwd.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: the test failed identically at the same assertion on two different trees, guard tree a14bffcdbf and clean base bd97664e07f78922f4f9803cb5688ba0b425f6fd, in the same long-path workspace and test environment (ToolRun 1ff97e7d77df29ca1443b8d36fbfb1d8). The cause is a fixed function of path length versus Rich's wrap width, not timing.

issue.creation_reason: The bob-cli-jf.1.2 guard verification found this sase publication-output test failing on the clean base too, because Rich wraps long checkout paths; no task tracks it.
